sanskrit.deva:
ता एता देवताः सृष्टा अस्मिन्महत्यर्णवे प्रापतन् ।
तमशनापिपासाभ्यामन्ववार्जत् ।
ता एनमब्रुवन्नायतनं नः प्रजानीहि ।
यस्मिन्प्रतिष्ठिता अन्नमदामेति ॥ १ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
tā etā devatāḥ sṛṣṭā asmin mahaty arṇave prāpatan |
tam aśanāpipāsābhyām anvavārjat |
tā enam abruvann āyatanaṃ naḥ prajānīhi |
yasmin pratiṣṭhitā annam adāmeti || 1 ||

lines.iast: tā etā devatāḥ sṛṣṭā asmin mahaty arṇave prāpatan
lines.deva: ता एता देवताः सृष्टा अस्मिन्महत्यर्णवे प्रापतन्

lines.iast: tā enam abruvann āyatanaṃ naḥ prajānīhi

padaccheda.iast: tāḥ etāḥ devatāḥ sṛṣṭāḥ asmin mahati arṇave prāpatan tam aśanā-pipāsābhyām anvavārjat tāḥ enam abruvan āyatanam naḥ prajānīhi yasmin pratiṣṭhitāḥ annam adāma iti
padaccheda.deva: ताः एताः देवताः सृष्टाः अस्मिन् महति अर्णवे प्रापतन् तम् अशना-पिपासाभ्याम् अन्ववार्जत् ताः एनम् अब्रुवन् आयतनम् नः प्रजानीहि यस्मिन् प्रतिष्ठिताः अन्नम् अदाम इति

translations.text: These deities, thus created, fell into this great ocean. He subjected him (that first-formed Puruṣa) to hunger and thirst. They said to him (the creator): ‘Provide for us an abode, established in which we may eat food.’

notes: Śaṅkara: the deities, fire and the rest, whom the Lord created with the intention that they should guard the worlds, fell into this great ocean of saṃsāra: whose water is the pain that springs from ignorance, desire and action; whose great sea-beasts are sharp disease, old age and death; without beginning, without end, shoreless, without support; where the only moment of rest is the drop of pleasure born of objects and senses; whose great waves are the hundreds of evils raised by the wind of thirst for the objects of the five senses; loud with the cries and wailing of those gone to the many hells, Mahāraurava and the rest; on which the raft is knowledge, stocked with the provisions of the virtues of the self, truth, uprightness, giving, compassion, non-injury, calm, restraint and firmness; whose course is the company of the good and the renunciation of all; and whose farther shore is liberation. Therefore even the end described before, the merging in fire and the other deities, which is the fruit of knowledge and rites performed together, is not enough to still the pain of saṃsāra: that is what is meant here. Since this is so, the supreme Brahman, the Self of oneself and of all beings, the cause of the origin, continuance and dissolution of the world, is to be known in order to still all the pain of saṃsāra: ‘this is the path, this the action, this Brahman, this the truth’ (Aitareya Āraṇyaka 2.1.1), ‘there is no other path for going’ (Śvetāśvatara 3.8, 6.15).

Śaṅkara: ‘him’ is that Puruṣa, the lump produced first, the seed from which seats, organs and deities arose; him he joined with hunger and thirst. Because he, the cause, has the faults of hunger and the like, the deities, his effects, have them too. Pressed by hunger and thirst they said to ‘him’, the grandfather, the creator: appoint for us a seat in which we shall be able to eat food.

sanskrit.deva:
ताभ्यो गामानयत् ।
ता अब्रुवन्न वै नोऽयमलमिति ।
ताभ्योऽश्वमानयत् ।
ता अब्रुवन्न वै नोऽयमलमिति ॥ २ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
tābhyo gām ānayat |
tā abruvan na vai no 'yam alam iti |
tābhyo 'śvam ānayat |
tā abruvan na vai no 'yam alam iti || 2 ||

lines.iast: tā abruvan na vai no 'yam alam iti
tā abruvan na vai no 'yam alam iti

padaccheda.iast: tābhyaḥ gām ānayat tāḥ abruvan na vai naḥ ayam alam iti tābhyaḥ aśvam ānayat tāḥ abruvan na vai naḥ ayam alam iti
padaccheda.deva: ताभ्यः गाम् आनयत् ताः अब्रुवन् न वै नः अयम् अलम् इति ताभ्यः अश्वम् आनयत् ताः अब्रुवन् न वै नः अयम् अलम् इति

translations.text: He brought them a cow. They said: ‘This is surely not enough for us.’ He brought them a horse. They said: ‘This is surely not enough for us.’

notes: Śaṅkara, introducing the mantra: the Lord, thus addressed.

Śaṅkara: a lump of the shape of a cow, drawn out from those same waters and given shape as before, he showed to them. Seeing the form of a cow they said: this lump is not enough for us as a seat in which to eat food; it is not fit for eating. The cow being refused, he brought them a horse, and they said the same.

sanskrit.deva:
ताभ्यः पुरुषमानयत् ।
ता अब्रुवन्सुकृतं बतेति ।
पुरुषो वाव सुकृतम् ।
ता अब्रवीद्यथायतनं प्रविशतेति ॥ ३ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
tābhyaḥ puruṣam ānayat |
tā abruvan sukṛtaṃ bateti |
puruṣo vāva sukṛtam |
tā abravīd yathāyatanaṃ praviśateti || 3 ||

padaccheda.iast: tābhyaḥ puruṣam ānayat tāḥ abruvan sukṛtam bata iti puruṣaḥ vāva sukṛtam tāḥ abravīt yathā-āyatanam praviśata iti
padaccheda.deva: ताभ्यः पुरुषम् आनयत् ताः अब्रुवन् सुकृतम् बत इति पुरुषः वाव सुकृतम् ताः अब्रवीत् यथा-आयतनम् प्रविशत इति

translations.text: He brought them a man. They said: ‘Ah, well made!’ Man indeed is what is well made. He said to them: ‘Enter, each into your own abode.’

notes: Śaṅkara, introducing the mantra: when all (the others) had been refused.

Śaṅkara: he brought them a man, who is of their own source. Seeing a man, their own source, they were no longer distressed and said: this seat is well made. Therefore man alone is ‘the well made’, because he is the cause of all meritorious action; or he is called sukṛta because he was made by (the Lord) himself (svayam), by his own powers of māyā. The Lord, thinking ‘this seat pleases them, for all delight in their own source’, said to them: enter each the abode that is fit for your own work, speaking and the rest.

sanskrit.deva:
अग्निर्वाग्भूत्वा मुखं प्राविशत् ।
वायुः प्राणो भूत्वा नासिके प्राविशत् ।
आदित्यश्चक्षुर्भूत्वाक्षिणी प्राविशत् ।
दिशः श्रोत्रं भूत्वा कर्णौ प्राविशन् ।
ओषधिवनस्पतयो लोमानि भूत्वा त्वचं प्राविशन् ।
चन्द्रमा मनो भूत्वा हृदयं प्राविशत् ।
मृत्युरपानो भूत्वा नाभिं प्राविशत् ।
आपो रेतो भूत्वा शिश्नं प्राविशन् ॥ ४ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
agnir vāg bhūtvā mukhaṃ prāviśat |
vāyuḥ prāṇo bhūtvā nāsike prāviśat |
ādityaś cakṣur bhūtvākṣiṇī prāviśat |
diśaḥ śrotraṃ bhūtvā karṇau prāviśan |
oṣadhivanaspatayo lomāni bhūtvā tvacaṃ prāviśan |
candramā mano bhūtvā hṛdayaṃ prāviśat |
mṛtyur apāno bhūtvā nābhiṃ prāviśat |
āpo reto bhūtvā śiśnaṃ prāviśan || 4 ||

padaccheda.iast: agniḥ vāk bhūtvā mukham prāviśat vāyuḥ prāṇaḥ bhūtvā nāsike prāviśat ādityaḥ cakṣuḥ bhūtvā akṣiṇī prāviśat diśaḥ śrotram bhūtvā karṇau prāviśan oṣadhi-vanaspatayaḥ lomāni bhūtvā tvacam prāviśan candramāḥ manaḥ bhūtvā hṛdayam prāviśat mṛtyuḥ apānaḥ bhūtvā nābhim prāviśat āpaḥ retaḥ bhūtvā śiśnam prāviśan
padaccheda.deva: अग्निः वाक् भूत्वा मुखम् प्राविशत् वायुः प्राणः भूत्वा नासिके प्राविशत् आदित्यः चक्षुः भूत्वा अक्षिणी प्राविशत् दिशः श्रोत्रम् भूत्वा कर्णौ प्राविशन् ओषधि-वनस्पतयः लोमानि भूत्वा त्वचम् प्राविशन् चन्द्रमाः मनः भूत्वा हृदयम् प्राविशत् मृत्युः अपानः भूत्वा नाभिम् प्राविशत् आपः रेतः भूत्वा शिश्नम् प्राविशन्

translations.text: Fire, having become speech, entered the mouth. Air, having become prāṇa, entered the nostrils. The sun, having become sight, entered the eyes. The quarters, having become hearing, entered the ears. Herbs and trees, having become hairs, entered the skin. The moon, having become mind, entered the heart. Death, having become apāna, entered the navel. The waters, having become seed, entered the generative organ.

notes: Śaṅkara, introducing the mantra: having received the Lord's leave, ‘so be it’, like the commanders of the army and other officers in a (king's) city.
Śaṅkara: fire, the deity that identifies itself with speech, became speech itself and entered its own source, the mouth. The rest is to be understood in the same way.

sanskrit.deva:
तमशनापिपासे अब्रूतामावाभ्यामभिप्रजानीहीति ।
ते अब्रवीदेतास्वेव वां देवतास्वाभजाम्येतासु भागिन्यौ करोमीति ।
तस्माद्यस्यै कस्यै च देवतायै हविर्गृह्यते भागिन्यावेवास्यामशनापिपासे भवतः ॥ ५ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
tam aśanāpipāse abrūtām āvābhyām abhiprajānīhīti |
te abravīd etāsv eva vāṃ devatāsv ābhajāmy etāsu bhāginyau karomīti |
tasmād yasyai kasyai ca devatāyai havir gṛhyate bhāginyāv evāsyām aśanāpipāse bhavataḥ || 5 ||

lines.iast: te abravīd etāsv eva vāṃ devatāsv ābhajāmy etāsu bhāginyau karomīti
lines.deva: ते अब्रवीदेतास्वेव वां देवतास्वाभजाम्येतासु भागिन्यौ करोमीति

lines.iast: tasmād yasyai kasyai ca devatāyai havir gṛhyate bhāginyāv evāsyām aśanāpipāse bhavataḥ
lines.deva: तस्माद्यस्यै कस्यै च देवतायै हविर्गृह्यते भागिन्यावेवास्यामशनापिपासे भवतः

padaccheda.iast: tam aśanā-pipāse abrūtām āvābhyām abhiprajānīhi iti te abravīt etāsu eva vām devatāsu ābhajāmi etāsu bhāginyau karomi iti tasmāt yasyai kasyai ca devatāyai haviḥ gṛhyate bhāginyau eva asyām aśanā-pipāse bhavataḥ
padaccheda.deva: तम् अशना-पिपासे अब्रूताम् आवाभ्याम् अभिप्रजानीहि इति ते अब्रवीत् एतासु एव वाम् देवतासु आभजामि एतासु भागिन्यौ करोमि इति तस्मात् यस्यै कस्यै च देवतायै हविः गृह्यते भागिन्यौ एव अस्याम् अशना-पिपासे भवतः

translations.text: Hunger and thirst said to him: ‘Provide (an abode) for us two.’ He said to them: ‘I give you a share in these very deities; I make you sharers in them.’ Therefore, for whatever deity an oblation is taken up, hunger and thirst are sharers in it.

notes: Śaṅkara, introducing the mantra: when the deities had thus obtained their seats.

Śaṅkara: hunger and thirst, being without a seat, said to the Lord: think of, appoint, a seat for us two. The Lord said to them: being states, you cannot be eaters of food without resting on something conscious; therefore I favour you with a part in the working of these very deities, fire and the rest, in the body and among the gods; whatever share, an oblation or the like, belongs to a deity, by that same share I make you two sharers. Because the Lord so ordained at the beginning of creation, even now, for whatever deity an oblation of boiled rice, cake or the like is taken up, hunger and thirst have a share in that deity.
The e-text reads avābhyām; it is set right here to āvābhyām, as the bhāṣya reads.
